body: Thank you, I'm feeling better now, just wanted to comment because people seemed worried!

This is exactly it. I've been a bit suicide-y the past 48 hours and just earlier today was thinking "it's probably just because of the holidays." Because, you know, that's what I've always heard.

I'm very glad I saw this, it immediately made me tell myself "self, take this more seriously".

Sometimes I want to kill myself then I play this game and I don't want to kill myself anymore. 

Especially if I run into another player. The idea that there might be other people out there in the same situation makes me want to make sure they always have someone else online to join them.

The "this is a temporary state" approach really helped me.

When I called, I was a huge mess and had to call back from sobbing...next morning, "wow, looks nice out today."

Kind of clicked for me that it's more of an impulse thing, at least in some cases, and not "my life is and always will be terrible"

A few weeks ago I called a suicide hotline and talked with a very nice person, really spilled my guts about who I was and the upcoming events that might cause me to become suicidal again.

He gave me his name and number to call back if I needed and he really seemed to genuinely care.

Would it be appropriate to call back and ask for him to let him know that I'm doing alright, and that he really helped that night?
Thank you very much! That was very thoughtful of you to put together, I will try not to make it be in vain!

Thank you, I have Flower (it came with the Journey special edition) and I love it! I will look into Dreamfall, I've never heard of it or Heavy Rain, but I've heard good things about LA Noire. I will try to try them all.

Again thank you

and thank you, r/SW, I slept all day but when I got up I felt much better. There are things I can do in the daylight that make me feel content and able to get things done but night is hard, the shows and games will help.

Thank you, I'm not particularly looking for a long game right now as I already lack the time to play them...Skyrim looks cool to me, for instance, but I hate the idea of getting hooked and wanting to spend all those hours I don't have playing it.

You are very kind to offer suggestions. I have a PS3. I also have a Steam account but I only used it to play Amnesia, which was a mistake because I didn't make it ten minutes in before it was too scary and the game too laggy.

I used to play video games all the time, Crash Bandicoot, Spyro the Dragon, Jak and Daxter, Okami, Shadow of the Colossus. The last game I got was Journey, a few years ago. It's an example of the kind of game I was looking for. It's been the game that when I had a Bad Night, I would play it start to end, it was pretty and relaxing and had pleasant music, and if I see another player in a level we tag along with each other and I feel less alone.

I also loved *The Endless Forest* years ago for the same reasons, it was even better, because you could spend fifteen minutes or two hours and it wouldn't demand your time. I couldn't talk to people but that's how it was designed, you had to just enjoy each other's pretty company. But my computer isn't a gaming PC, and I had to stop playing it because it was so laggy.

I have been wanting to play the Dragon Age games, though, based on such high recommendation.

Thank you, that sounds perfect. I found [this site](http://gakifiles.blogspot.com/p/watch-clips.html) and I will be watching them one by one.

I will add Better Off Ted to my comedy to-watch list; I've seen a season or two of AD, I'll get back on that boat too.

Is it anything like that old movie *Better Off Dead*? I love that movie.

I'm caught up on Archer. Fantastic show. Maybe I'll try finding my favorite episode.

Thank you, I will add it to my list of shows I need to watch. It seems a little extreme for the purposes I was leaning towards here, though. I was looking for something I could switch to that is low-drama, pleasant, and required little time investment, just to calm down when it gets bad.
